name: Woolly Hair-Palmoplantar Keratoderma Syndrome

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical Diagnostic Criteria for Woolly Hair-Palmoplantar Keratoderma Syndrome

criteria.description: Presence of tightly curled, fine, and brittle hair resembling woolly hair
Diffuse or focal thickening of the skin on palms and soles (palmoplantar keratoderma)
Positive family history consistent with autosomal recessive inheritance
Absence of cardiomyopathy or arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy (to exclude related syndromes)

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of both woolly hair and palmoplantar keratoderma with supportive family history or genetic confirmation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing for mutations in desmosomal genes (e.g., DSP, JUP) can confirm diagnosis

pathognomonic.symptomName: Woolly hair phenotype characterized by tightly curled, fragile hair

searchTerms: thickened skin on palms and soles

common.symptomName: Hyperlinearity of the palms and soles
searchTerms: extra lines on palms and soles
increased skin lines on hands and feet

common.symptomName: Nail dystrophy including thickened and brittle nails
Mild erythema and scaling on palms and soles
searchTerms: mild redness and scaling on hands and feet
dry scaly skin on palms and soles

common.symptomName: Hair shaft fragility leading to hair breakage

searchTerms: thickened skin around mouth and eyes
scaly skin plaques on face edges

occasional.symptomName: Mild palmoplantar pain or discomfort due to keratoderma
searchTerms: mild pain on palms and soles

occasional.symptomName: Hypohidrosis or reduced sweating on palms and soles
searchTerms: reduced sweating on hands and feet
less sweat production on palms and soles

occasional.symptomName: Transient erythematous patches on trunk or limbs
searchTerms: brief red skin areas on trunk or limbs

rare.symptomName: Cardiac arrhythmias without structural heart disease
Alopecia or patchy hair loss beyond woolly hair

laboratory: Histopathology of palmoplantar skin showing hyperkeratosis with acanthosis
Hair microscopy revealing twisted and irregular hair shafts
imaging: Echocardiography typically normal but recommended to exclude cardiomyopathy
other: Family pedigree analysis consistent with autosomal recessive inheritance

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy
Woolly hair and palmoplantar keratoderma with cardiac involvement
Woolly hair and palmoplantar keratoderma with early-onset heart failure
Uncombable, spangled hair without palmoplantar keratoderma
No associated cardiac or skin thickening features

redFlags: Development of cardiac arrhythmias or cardiomyopathy
Rapid progression of palmoplantar keratoderma with pain or fissuring
Signs of systemic infection or secondary skin infection due to keratoderma
references: Norgett EE, et al. Mutations in desmoplakin cause woolly hair and palmoplantar keratoderma. Nat Genet. 2000.
McKoy G, et al. Identification of a deletion in plakoglobin in arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy with palmoplantar keratoderma and woolly hair (Naxos disease). Lancet. 2000.
Orphanet: Woolly hair-palmoplantar keratoderma syndrome. ORPHA:420686.
